body.statement: For every finite \(\mathcal H_0\subset[-H,H]^K\), the fixed Gaussian grid experiment is exactly embedded by vertex controls in the score diffusion, and the strict extension from the regular-payoff results of Wager and Xu and Adusumilli holds: arbitrary predictable policies, zero-allocation faces, and the discontinuous closed-test terminal loss satisfy \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|\to0\), \(c_{n,m}\to c_m\) for every \(m\), and \(V_n\to V\). Moreover, for each \(\epsilon>0\) there are predictable finite-horizon policies whose scenario-risk vectors converge coordinatewise to that of an \(\epsilon\)-optimal diffusion control.
body.justification: It identifies the attainable local-power regret frontier for the fixed confirmatory test.
body.gap: Adusumilli's 2026 theorem gives subsequential allocation-process representations and Adusumilli's 2025 convergence theorem uses Hölder data; this theorem adds a discontinuous closure payoff and legal boundary atoms.
body.consumer: It converts a continuum recruitment solution into asymptotically valid finite-stage policies for interAdapt-style designs.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary finite scenario list \(\mathcal H_0=\{h^1,\ldots,h^M\}\subset[-H,H]^K\).  The proof below uses only this finiteness and the coordinate bound \(|h_j^m|\leq H\); it never invokes coordinatewise null-boundary closure.

\emph{Exact embedding.}
Fix \(n\) and \(\pi_n\in\Pi_n\).  On
\(((i-1)/n,i/n]\), let the continuous control be the vertex
\[
u_j(t)=\mathbf 1\{A_i=j\}.
\]
The action \(A_i\) is chosen at the left endpoint from the observed past.  It is therefore predictable by Assumption
\(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\mbox{-}predictability}\), and the resulting piecewise-constant control belongs to \(\mathcal U\) by Assumption
\(\mathrm{ass{:}continuous\mbox{-}observed\mbox{-}control}\) and Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}continuous\mbox{-}control\mbox{-}class}\).
Conditionally on the history and \(A_i=j\), its score increment is
\[
\Delta X_j=\frac{h_j^m}{n}
+W_j(i/n)-W_j((i-1)/n)
\sim\mathcal N(h_j^m/n,1/n),
\]
and its clock increment is \(1/n\); all other coordinates have zero
increments.  By Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\mbox{-}known\mbox{-}variance}\)
and \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\mbox{-}scenario\mbox{-}scaling}\),
\(Y_i/\sqrt n\) has exactly this conditional law.  Induction over \(i\)
therefore gives equality of the complete observed score-clock laws under every
scenario \(m\), not merely weak convergence.  Thus every finite policy is a
vertex-control diffusion policy and has exactly the same scenario-risk vector.

\emph{Approximation for continuous terminal payoffs.}
Let \(g_m:\mathbb R^K\times[0,1]^K\to[0,1]\) be bounded and continuous,
for \(m=1,\ldots,M\).  We show that the infimal prior-weighted risk over the
embedded \(n\)-grid controls converges to the infimum over \(\mathcal U\).

On the canonical observed space, every progressively measurable
\(\Delta(\mathcal J)\)-valued control is approximable in
\(dt\,d\mathbb P_0\)-measure by simple predictable controls: approximate
indicators in the predictable sigma-field by finite unions of left-cylinder
sets, approximate the bounded simplex coordinates by simple functions, and
project onto the closed simplex.  Boundedness upgrades convergence in measure
to
\[
\mathbb E_0\int_0^1\sum_j|u_j^{(r)}(t)-u_j(t)|\,dt\longrightarrow0.
\tag{1}
\]
For a fixed simple control, subdivide each of its time cells into \(n\)-grid
cells and, conditionally on the information at the left endpoint, choose
vertex \(j\) with its declared simplex probability.  The sum of the conditional
variances of the normalized centered allocation counts is at most \(1/n\), so
the cumulative clock error tends to zero in probability.  Conditional on
those counts, the score increment in coordinate \(j\) is Gaussian with mean
\(h_j^m\Delta Q_j\) and variance \(\Delta Q_j\).  Therefore its conditional
characteristic function is
\[
\exp\!\left\{\mathrm i z_jh_j^m\Delta Q_j
-\frac12z_j^2\Delta Q_j\right\},
\]
which converges to the characteristic function of the corresponding relaxed
Gaussian transition.  Induction over the finitely many simple-control cells
proves joint convergence of the terminal score and clock.  Past-measurable
simple functions may be chosen continuous outside sets of arbitrarily small
probability simultaneously under the finitely many scenario laws; changing
them on those sets changes a bounded risk by at most that probability.  A
diagonal choice in \(r\) and \(n\) therefore gives grid policies
\(\pi_n[u]\) such that
\[
(X_n,Q_n)\ \Longrightarrow\ (X^u(1),Q^u(1))
\quad\text{under every }m.
\tag{2}
\]
This construction uses vertex choices even when some simplex coordinates
are zero, so it imposes no exploration lower bound.

The transfer from the zero-drift reference law to every scenario is uniform.
The assignment factors cancel because the policy is scenario independent,
and the Gaussian likelihood ratio is
\[
Z_m(X,Q)=
\exp\!\left\{\sum_jh_j^mX_j-\frac12
\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_j\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Conditioning successively on score increments gives
\[
\mathbb E_0[Z_m(X,Q)^2]
=\mathbb E_0\exp\!\left\{\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_j\right\}
\leq\exp(H^2),
\tag{4}
\]
because \(\sum_jQ_j=1\) and \(|h_j^m|\leq H\).  Thus the likelihood ratios
are uniformly integrable, and reference-law convergence transfers to all
\(M\) scenario laws.  Equations (1)--(4), bounded continuity of \(g_m\),
and an arbitrarily near-optimal choice of \(u\) show, for every
\(\lambda\in\Delta_M\),
\[
\inf_{\pi_n\in\Pi_n}\sum_m\lambda_m\mathbb E_m^{\pi_n}g_m
\longrightarrow
\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_m\lambda_m\mathbb E_m^ug_m.
\tag{5}
\]
The lower-bound direction in (5) holds for every \(n\), because exact
embedding makes the finite grid class a subclass of the continuous-control
class.  Hence this regular-payoff approximation is derived from the primitive
Gaussian transitions.

For fixed \(\delta>0\), the functions
\(\ell_{m,\delta}^{\pm}\) in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}terminal\mbox{-}envelopes}\) are bounded and continuous:
exponentiation, finite averages, and finite minima are continuous, as are
\(f_\delta^\pm\).  Applying (5) yields
\[
B_{n,\delta}^\pm(\lambda)\longrightarrow
B_\delta^\pm(\lambda).
\tag{6}
\]
Every value in (6) is \(1\)-Lipschitz in \(\lambda\) for the
\(\ell_1\) norm, because every scenario risk is in \([0,1]\).  Cover compact
\(\Delta_M\) by a finite \(\ell_1\)-net, apply pointwise convergence at the
net points, and use the two Lipschitz bounds.  This upgrades (6) to convergence
uniform in \(\lambda\).

\emph{Removal of the continuous envelopes.}
The scalar bracketing in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\mbox{-}terminal\mbox{-}comparison}\) gives
\[
B_{n,\delta}^-(\lambda)\leq B_n(\lambda)\leq
B_{n,\delta}^+(\lambda),
\qquad
B_\delta^-(\lambda)\leq B(\lambda)\leq B_\delta^+(\lambda).
\]
Combining these inequalities with uniform convergence in (6) gives
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}
|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|
\leq\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\sqrt\delta).
\]
Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) and using the final conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\mbox{-}terminal\mbox{-}comparison}\) proves
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]
For the point-mass prior \(e_m\), the definitions give
\(B_n(e_m)=c_{n,m}\) and \(B(e_m)=c_m\).  Hence (7) proves
\[
\max_{1\leq m\leq M}|c_{n,m}-c_m|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]

For completeness, we derive the finite-scenario minimax identity needed to
pass from (7)--(8) to regret values.  Let \(C_n\) be the closure in
\([0,1]^M\) of the achievable regret vectors.  Independent randomization at
time zero makes it convex, and closure makes it compact without changing the
infimum of a continuous criterion.  Since
\(\max_m r_m=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\lambda^\top r\), finite-dimensional
convex separation gives
\[
\inf_{r\in C_n}\max_mr_m
=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\inf_{r\in C_n}\lambda^\top r.
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, let \(v=\inf_{r\in C_n}\max_mr_m\).  The upward-closed convex set
\(C_n+\mathbb R_+^M\) has \(v\mathbf1\) on its boundary.  Projecting
\((v-k^{-1})\mathbf1\) onto this set and taking a convergent subsequence of
the normalized projection normals produces \(\lambda\geq0\),
\(\sum_m\lambda_m=1\), with \(\lambda^\top r\geq v\) for every
\(r\in C_n\).  The opposite inequality follows from
\(\lambda^\top r\leq\max_mr_m\), proving (9).
Translating from regret to loss yields
\[
V_n=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}
\left\{B_n(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{n,m}\right\},
\]
and the identical argument gives the corresponding formula for \(V\).
Consequently,
\[
|V_n-V|
\leq\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|
+\max_m|c_{n,m}-c_m|\longrightarrow0
\]
by (7)--(8).

\emph{Predictable policy attainment.}
Fix \(\epsilon>0\).  Choose \(N\) so large that
\(|V_N-V|+\max_m|c_{N,m}-c_m|<\epsilon/3\), and choose
\(\pi_N\in\Pi_N\) with
\[
\max_m\{L_N(\pi_N,m)-c_{N,m}\}\leq V_N+\epsilon/3.
\]
Embed \(\pi_N\) as the \(N\)-block vertex control \(u^\epsilon\) constructed
above.  Exact equality of risk vectors and the preceding bounds show
\[
\max_m r_m(u^\epsilon)\leq V+\epsilon.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus \(u^\epsilon\) is an \(\epsilon\)-optimal diffusion control.

It remains to approximate this particular control for the original
discontinuous loss.  Conditional on an exogenous random seed and on any of
the finitely many action sequences of \(\pi_N\), the sampled Gaussian block
increments have a Lebesgue density.  Every terminal threshold equality is
contained in a finite union of zero sets of
\[
\sum_{j\in I}\exp(X_j-Q_j/2)-20|I|.
\]
This analytic function is nonconstant whenever one of its coordinates was
sampled; if none was sampled, its value is \(|I|-20|I|\neq0\).
Its zero set therefore has Lebesgue measure zero.  Hence
\[
\Pr_m^{u^\epsilon}\{a_j(X(1),Q(1))=0
\text{ for some }j\}=0
\quad\text{for every }m.
\tag{11}
\]
At horizon \(n\), divide enrollment into \(N\) consecutive blocks whose
lengths differ from \(n/N\) by at most one, keep the arm selected by
\(\pi_N\) throughout a block, and feed the next decision the normalized
block aggregate.  This is a predictable finite policy.  Each aggregate is
exactly Gaussian with clock length converging to \(1/N\); induction over the
fixed number \(N\) of blocks gives convergence of its terminal state to that
of \(u^\epsilon\).  Arbitrary measurable recruitment kernels of \(\pi_N\)
may first be changed on sets of arbitrarily small probability under the
finite family of Gaussian history laws so that this induction is valid at
their continuity points.  Equation (11) then permits the bounded
continuous-mapping argument for the strict miss indicators.  Thus the
resulting predictable policies \(\pi_n^\epsilon\) satisfy
\[
L_n(\pi_n^\epsilon,m)\longrightarrow L(u^\epsilon,m)
\quad\text{for every }m.
\]
Together with (10), this proves the asserted coordinatewise risk transfer.
The construction admits zero block allocations to unused subgroups.  Every
argument above is internal to the declared finite list \(\mathcal H_0\);
the common-drift perturbation used by the terminal-comparison lemma is only a
change-of-measure device and does not require any translated or projected
scenario to belong to that list.
